bull_bear.body:
- Fully integrated manufacturing capability spanning tooling, forging and machining, enabling high-volume production with consistent quality and cost optimisation
- In-house metallurgical and metrological capabilities supporting precision, quality control and continuous product/process innovation
- Manufacturing facilities located close to key customers, improving supply-chain responsiveness, logistics cost and delivery reliability
- Long-standing, diversified global OEM customer base (Dana, John Deere, Kubota, Meritor, Mahindra & Mahindra, Escorts, TAFE, International Tractors, Automotive/Axles India, Claas) across 12 countries and 30 Indian states, indicating high switching costs
- Robotics-supported forging facilities and ongoing automation investment underpinning cost and accuracy advantages
- Centralised sourcing/vendor management for raw material (steel) procurement giving economies of scale
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff / trade-policy exposure on exports — Exports to the USA were highly impacted by tariffs imposed by the US Government during FY2025-26, driving an overall drop of around 4% in total sales; management flags that any further increase or new imposition of US tariffs can adversely impact export revenues and demand for the Company's products in the US Commercial Vehicle market.
- Dependence on OEM customer demand, both domestic and export — The Company's business is heavily dependent on demand from OEM customers (tractor and commercial vehicle manufacturers) in India and abroad; a slowdown among these customers directly affects the Company's volumes and top line.
- Geographic/export revenue concentration — A material share of revenue comes from exports (North America, Europe and other overseas markets), exposing the Company to demand slowdowns, currency and trade-policy shifts in those specific geographies.
- Single-business-segment concentration — The Company operates in a single business segment (manufacturing automobile components), with no separate segment reporting; diversification into LV/PV/EV components via GNA Mobility Limited is only in its early, pre-operational stage.
- Geopolitical and global macroeconomic uncertainty — Management notes escalating geopolitical tensions (including in West Asia), a fragile global economy entering CY2026, higher policy uncertainty, and volatile trade/tariff conditions as factors that could affect demand and the Company's operations.
- Cyclicality tied to tractor and commercial vehicle demand drivers — Demand for the Company's core products is closely linked to factors such as monsoon performance, GST rates on tractors, and government infrastructure/agriculture spending, making revenue sensitive to these external and seasonal drivers.
- Raw material (steel) sourcing dependency — The Company relies on centralised sourcing and vendor management for raw material procurement, especially steel, indicating exposure to steel price and supply conditions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Deliberate shift from volume-led growth to a more durable, value-driven business through disciplined execution and improved cost structures
- Reshaping the product portfolio towards higher-value opportunities, expanding presence in Light Vehicles (LV) and Passenger Vehicles (PV) for stronger realisations and long-term demand visibility
- Building capabilities in advanced components for light vehicles, passenger vehicles and electric vehicles through GNA Mobility Limited to prepare for the next phase of mobility
- Expanding market reach into SUV and LCV axle shaft segments to reduce dependence on traditional HCV/MHCV/tractor segments and broaden the global footprint across North America, Europe and Asia

- Exhibiting integrated manufacturing strength across tooling, machining and forging to drive economies of scale and cost optimisation

- Accelerating investment in advanced machining and automation to enhance throughput, precision and cost efficiency

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: GNA Axles operates two manufacturing units in Punjab (Mehtiana, Hoshiarpur and Gulab Garh Jattan, Kapurthala). Historically, the Company built out a new forging shop and an SUV axle machining line (construction initiated 2017), opened a new machine shop for off-highway axle shafts (2018), initiated setting up of an SUV plant (2019) and commenced production at the SUV plant (2023); overall installed capacity was increased to 6.7 million components in 2021-22. In 2025 the Company incorporated GNA Mobility Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, to expand into a broader automotive components range covering light vehicles, passenger vehicles and electric vehicles; in 2026 GNA Mobility approved an investment plan of Rs 800 Cr for this expansion. On the renewable-energy side, the Company commissioned a 1.4 MW rooftop solar power project in 2024, expanded rooftop solar capacity to 6 MW by the close of FY2025-26, and has initiated a new 10 MW solar park project at Thikriwal village, Kapurthala district, Punjab. The Company also continues to invest in advanced machining and automation to enhance throughput, precision and cost efficiency.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Robust domestic tractor and commercial vehicle demand helped limit the downside in the top line even as exports were hit by US tariffs
- Lowering of GST rate on tractors coupled with an above-normal monsoon supported industry demand
- Rising non-farm use of tractors (haulage, construction, sand mining, rural infrastructure work) has increased demand for the Company's products
- Exports declined due to US tariffs, driving an overall ~4% drop in total sales for the year
- Export sales improved in the last quarter of FY2025-26 as US tariffs were lowered and rationalised, with India engaging on a bilateral trade deal to avoid reciprocal tariffs
- As global automakers reduce reliance on traditional sourcing hubs, India has an opportunity to increase direct exports
- SUV segment penetration has already started yielding results and is identified as the Company's next growth engine, in both domestic and overseas markets
- Promising GDP growth outlook, government incentives for manufacturing/agriculture productivity, and continued infrastructure focus are expected to improve demand for CVs and Tractors
- Management remains optimistic on domestic demand while watching geopolitical developments, interest rates, fuel prices and inflation; adverse tariff developments in the USA remain a watch item for CV demand

Any increase in or new imposition of US tariffs could adversely impact the Company's export revenues and demand for its products from the US Commercial Vehicle market.

Through GNA Mobility Limited, the Company will build capabilities in advanced components for light vehicles, passenger vehicles and electric vehicles to remain relevant as the automotive space evolves.
Company intends to invest in automation for most stages of the production process to improve resource use and manufacturing accuracy.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
